claims.claim: Every connected cograph other than a singleton or a graph with exactly one universal vertex is equivalent to the zero game.
claims.evidence: A connected non-singleton cograph has a join decomposition. Two universal vertices x,y give N[x]∩N[y]=V, hence one pairing-dominating pair. If there is no universal vertex, there are at least two join blocks and each has at least two vertices. Choosing a,b in one block and c,d in another makes (c,d) cover the first block and (a,b) cover every other block. Remark 9 therefore makes the component contextually zero. These cases exhaust the non-exceptions.
claims.witness: Pairing certificates {(x,y)} and {(a,b),(c,d)}. Direct minimax also returned (0,0) for all 1,199 applicable connected labeled cographs through six vertices.
claims.search_method: Deductive join-decomposition analysis from the authorized source and draft, followed by exhaustive labeled-cograph minimax; no web or other evidence was used.

claims.claim: SHVG on cographs is polynomially equivalent to an explicit open-or-delete scoring game on rooted forests.
claims.evidence: For a unique universal vertex u, swapping the first local move x with u is valid in every disjoint context. In Maker's swap, either both x,u ultimately belong to Maker or the shadow position gives u to Breaker and hence scores zero in that component, while the swapped play is nonnegative. The dual swap is no worse for Breaker because actually taking u makes the component score zero. If Breaker takes u, the residual position has both scores zero. If Maker takes u, C-u has at least two vertices and contains twins a,b. Applying Theorem 13 to assign a to Maker and b to Breaker in both C and C-u makes u permanently spoiled, while every vertex of C-u has identical happiness in the two positions. Induction therefore gives the open/expose and delete transitions contextually. Conversely, recursively adjoining a universal vertex to the child union plus a zero K2 ballast realizes every internal forest node as a cograph; it uses O(N) vertices and polynomial explicit size.
claims.witness: Exact direct SHVG minimax agreed with the recursively reduced open-or-delete forest for all 6,039 labeled cographs through six vertices.
claims.search_method: Context-preserving strategy transposition, twin reduction, structural induction, and exhaustive comparison against unrestricted graph play; no web used.

claims.claim: The cograph game is linear-time solvable when every tree in the reduced forest has outdegree at most two.
claims.evidence: Inductively replace each child by prize A or zero Z. After omitting Z children, an internal node with zero or one A child has starting scores (0,0), so Theorem 6 makes it Z. With two A children, opening exposes A+A, which is the constant game 1, while deletion yields zero; these are exactly A's two options. Thus every binary subtree is contextually A or Z, and the forest reduces to z prizes with scores ceil(z/2) and floor(z/2). One postorder pass labels all reduced-forest nodes, so the computation is linear in that representation and in a linear-size cotree representation.
claims.witness: All 398 unlabeled rooted trees through ten nodes with outdegree at most two matched their A/Z label, including 9,950 score-pair comparisons after adjoining generated contexts.
claims.search_method: Structural induction on rooted trees plus exhaustive contextual minimax checks; no web used.

claims.claim: Reduced forests of height one—equivalently, disjoint unions of stars and isolated vertices after zero components are removed—admit an O(n^2) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: The unrestricted recurrence considers taking an exposed prize, opening any star, or deleting any star. A joint exchange induction on the remaining roots and prizes shows that replacing a smaller unopened star by a larger one cannot lower Maker's value and that opening the larger while retaining the smaller is at least as favorable as the reverse. Hence Maker may open and Breaker may delete the largest remaining star, yielding exactly the displayed two recurrences. The invariant l+sum(remaining leaf counts)≤K gives O(rK)=O(n^2) states, with constant-time transitions after sorting.
claims.witness: The largest-star recurrence agreed with unrestricted minimax over all 65,065 generated states having up to six unopened stars, leaf counts through eight, and up to twelve exposed prizes.
claims.search_method: Derived the all-moves recurrence, checked the exchange inequalities casewise, and exhaustively compared restricted versus unrestricted choices; no web used.

claims.claim: If q is the number of vertices of outdegree at least three in a reduced rooted forest, every residual forest occurring in play is equivalent, up to the integer score already secured, to a branching-core state (S,l), where l counts prize-leaf games and S is an antichain of at most q original nodes, each rooting a remaining component that contains a branching vertex.
claims.evidence: Every subtree containing no branching vertex has outdegree at most two and is contextually A or Z by claim 2. Replacing all such active components leaves prize count l and roots S whose subtrees contain branching vertices. Active roots are always incomparable original nodes. Their rooted subtrees are disjoint, so assigning one contained branching vertex to each root injects S into the q branching vertices and proves |S|≤q. Opening a root replaces it by its marked children and corresponding A children; deleting it removes its whole subtree. These transitions preserve the invariant and enumerate every legal move.
claims.witness: Full open-or-delete minimax and branching-core minimax agreed on 2,173 generated single-tree and mixed-forest instances through the tested size bounds.
claims.search_method: Invariant and injection proof on original forest nodes, supplemented by exact exhaustive minimax; no web used.

claims.claim: The rooted-forest game, and hence SHVG on cographs, has an exact XP algorithm parameterized by q, the number of outdegree-at-least-three vertices in the reduced forest; in particular it is polynomial-time solvable for every fixed q.
claims.evidence: The two recurrences list exactly the prize move and every active-root move for the appropriate player. Taking a prize, deleting a subtree, or opening a root strictly decreases the measure consisting of active original subtree nodes plus l; when opening, every replacement prize accounts for a nonempty discarded subtree and the root itself disappears. Thus memoization is acyclic. Since l≤n and S is a subset of at most q original nodes, there are at most (n+1)∑_{i=0}^q binom(n,i) states. At most q+1 transitions with O(q) tuple work per state give the asserted XP bound, and polynomial cograph reduction preserves exact scores.
claims.witness: The checker independently compared the claimed core recurrence with unrestricted play on 2,173 generated forests, including mixed contexts.
claims.search_method: Recurrence completeness, well-founded-measure, and state-count analysis, with exact finite cross-checks; no web used.

claims.claim: The pair of standalone scores (Ms,Bs) is insufficient as a cotree dynamic-programming state.
claims.evidence: P3 and K1,3 reduce respectively to S2 and S3, and each has standalone scores (1,0). Nevertheless, direct recurrence gives scores (1,1) for S2+S2 and (2,1) for S2+S3. Replacing one component by another with the same score pair can therefore change a union-node result, ruling out that pair as a complete compositional cotree state.
claims.search_method: Exact symbolic evaluation and direct integer minimax; no web used.

claims.claim: For every m≥1, the rooted stars S_{2m} and S_{2m+1} have the same standalone scores (m,0), but adjoining one prize leaf A gives scores (m,1) and (m+1,1), respectively.
claims.evidence: Maker opening S_k leaves Breaker on k prizes, giving floor(k/2), while Breaker deletes the star for zero. In A+S_k, Maker's alternatives have values 1 and floor((k+1)/2), while Breaker's alternatives leave Maker S_k or A, giving min(floor(k/2),1). Substitution at k=2m and 2m+1 yields exactly (m,1) and (m+1,1), with the m≥1 condition handling the minimum.
claims.witness: The four asserted score formulas were checked exactly for every 1≤m≤30.
claims.search_method: Closed-form evaluation of all legal root choices plus exact integer minimax; no web used.

claims.claim: For every N there are N pairwise contextually inequivalent rooted-tree games on at most 2N+4 forest nodes that all have standalone scores (1,0); thus the failure of the (Ms,Bs) state is unbounded.
claims.evidence: For F_m with children A,A,S_{2m}, the node count is 2m+4. Breaker deletes its root for zero; Maker opens it and leaves Breaker on the constant 1 plus S_{2m}, giving one. Thus every F_m has (1,0). For r<s, context S_{2s} gives Breaker-first value 1. Maker can open S_{2s} for value s or F_r for value r+1, so Ms(F_r+S_{2s})=s; replacing F_r by F_s makes the latter option s+1. This single context separates each pair, and m=1,…,N respects the node bound.
claims.witness: For r<s, S_{2s} distinguishes F_r and F_s by Maker-first scores s versus s+1. The checker verified all such pairs through s=20.
claims.search_method: Explicit contextual score calculation and exact integer minimax; no web used.

target_evidence: The source target asks for an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm on all cographs or a matching hardness theorem. The XP algorithm is polynomial only for fixed q, while q may grow with the input; the contextual obstruction rules out only the two-score summary and proves no complexity lower bound. The draft therefore does not fully classify the unrestricted problem. Its exact reduction, tractable subclasses, fixed-q algorithm, and unbounded state obstruction are nevertheless material correct progress. The parent's PARTIAL label and explicit statement that the unrestricted target remains open are accurate.
